interpretation: Refutes the leading hypothesis: with the entire backbone provably frozen/unchanged, LIBERO-Spatial got WORSE (73.33%->16.67%) not better. Re-diagnosis: action_encoder/head are shared weight matrices whose column/row ranges overlap between LIBERO (0-6) and RoboTwin (0-13) -- RoboTwin's gradient directly updates the same columns LIBERO depends on, and with the backbone frozen there is no downstream plasticity to compensate. Points to per-embodiment-separated projection weights (not a shared K=14 projection) as the next fix.
modifications: Added Trainer.trainable_modules=expanded_projections_only: freeze entire shared MoT backbone, train only action_encoder/head/proprio_encoder (6 tensors)

what_to_watch: Whether LIBERO retention improves vs exp0001; whether RoboTwin still shows zero learning with fewer trainable params.
why_this_might_help: Investigation of exp0001 hypothesized the unmasked video loss trains the shared backbone on RoboTwin's different visual domain, hurting LIBERO; freezing the backbone should isolate/prevent this.

interpretation: Result contradicts the simple disjoint-offset-fixes-it hypothesis: with the same trainable-backbone treatment as exp0001, disjoint projection offsets should have produced retention >= exp0001's 73.33% if projection-column overlap were the sole interference mechanism. Instead it landed at 50.00%, worse than exp0001, better than exp0002. Per-task pattern is scattered/task-swapping rather than a uniform decline (3 tasks fine in exp0001 dropped to 0%, 3 different tasks weak in exp0001 hit 100%), consistent with either meaningful run-to-run variance on a small 3-trial/task panel or a new instability source from RoboTwin's all-fresh-init projection weights (vs exp0001's partial warm-start via reused/corrupted LIBERO weights). Combined with exp0002 (backbone freezing alone also failed), points toward the shared transformer backbone as an under-isolated interference channel -- no candidate so far has combined disjoint projections with a frozen backbone to test this cleanly. Recommends investigate-fastwam-problem before the next candidate.

A disjoint per-embodiment offset makes this provably interference-free (see gradient-isolation unit test) without the much larger implementation risk of fully separate per-embodiment weight matrices.
